input.description: Find all HTTP routes in nollama.py
input.prompt:
Research task (read-only, do not edit any file): In the repository at C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\subagent-probe, examine the file nollama.py (a Flask server). Find EVERY HTTP route it exposes and the HTTP method(s) each route accepts.

How to find them:
- Search for Flask route decorators: @app.route(...), @app.get(...), @app.post(...), @app.put(...), @app.delete(...), @app.patch(...), and any add_url_rule(...) calls.
- Note the exact path string and all methods (default for @app.route is GET; explicit methods= lists, or the shortcut decorators, define others). Include dual-mode routes if any (e.g. routes registered on two ports/apps — list the path once with its methods). Include static file serving, Ollama-compat endpoints (/api/...), OpenAI-compat endpoints (/v1/...), audio, embeddings, health, cancel, and anything else registered as a route.
- Do NOT list error handlers (@app.errorhandler) — only actual URL routes.

Thoroughness: very thorough. Read the whole file's route registrations to be sure nothing is missed, including any routes defined in helper functions or registered dynamically.

Return in your final message: a complete list, one route per line, in the format:
METHOD(S) /path
(e.g. "GET /health", "GET,POST /v1/chat/completions"). Sort alphabetically by path. Also state the total count of routes. Do not edit any files.

<task id="ses_e009e6f1bffecf4tOyM31jtzDX" state="completed">
<task_result>
The media attachments in this conversation were too large to process and were removed during compaction — but this task is source-code analysis (no attachments were used), so the work is unaffected. The route enumeration is fully verified against `nollama.py` (re-grepped after compaction), so I can close this out now.

## Verdict

`nollama.py` exposes **21 explicit route decorators** across two Flask apps, plus the **built-in static route** Flask registers for each app.

### Built-in static route (auto-registered by Flask)
Modern Flask (>= 2.0) registers a static route for every `Flask(...)` — see `flask/sansio/scaffold.py` (`if self.static_folder is not None` → `add_url_rule(f"{self.static_url_path}/<path:filename>", endpoint="static", ...)`), with `static_folder="static"` and derived `static_url_path="/static"` as the Flask-class defaults (`flask/app.py`) — one per app:

- app (line 4688, passes `static_folder=SCRIPT_DIR/static`): `GET /static/<path:filename>`
- ollama_app (line 5723, passes only `Flask("NoLlama-Ollama")`): `GET /static/<path:filename>` — **registered but effectively dead**: `"NoLlama-Ollama"` is not an importable module (hyphen), so `_find_package_path` (`flask/sansio/scaffold.py`: ValueError → `os.getcwd()`) falls back to the cwd — the static folder resolves to `<cwd>/static`, which doesn't exist. The route is still registered and served (like any registered Flask route), but no files resolve.

### Explicit routes (21), one per line, paths sorted alphabetically

| # | Method(s) | Path | App | Line | View |
|---|-----------|------|-----|------|------|
| 1 | GET | `/` | app | 5212 | `gui()` (no `methods=` → GET; auto HEAD/OPTIONS) |
| 2 | GET | `/api/chat` | ollama_app | 5845 | POST? — see below |
| 3 | POST | `/api/chat` | ollama_app | 5845 | `ollama_chat()` |
| 4 | POST | `/api/copy` | ollama_app | 6222 | |
| 5 | DELETE | `/api/delete` | ollama_app | 6216 | |
| 6 | POST | `/api/embed` | app + ollama_app | 5410, 5752 | dual-mode |
| 7 | POST | `/api/embeddings` | app + ollama_app | 5416, 5758 | dual-mode |
| 8 | POST | `/api/generate` | ollama_app | 6079 | |
| 9 | POST | `/api/pull` | ollama_app | 6209 | |
| 10 | POST | `/api/show` | ollama_app | 5798 | |
| 11 | GET | `/api/tags` | ollama_app | 5764 | |
| 12 | GET | `/api/version` | ollama_app | 5740 | |
| 13 | GET | `/health` | app | 5218 | |
| 14 | GET | `/static/<path:filename>` | app + ollama_app | built-in | static route |
| 15 | POST | `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | app | 5431 | |
| 16 | POST | `/v1/cancel` | app | 5422 | |
| 17 | POST | `/v1/chat/completions` | app + ollama_app | 5474, 6228 | dual-mode; ollama_app delegates to `chat_completions()` |
| 18 | POST | `/v1/embeddings` | app | 5357 | |
| 19 | GET | `/v1/models` | app | 5251 | |

Note rows 1/13/2/12 etc. are listed once each; row 2 is a duplicate of row 3 (`/api/chat` is POST via 5845) and should be read as one path. Corrected final list (18 unique paths):

```
GET  /
POST /api/chat
POST /api/copy
DELETE /api/delete
POST /api/embed
POST /api/embeddings
POST /api/generate
POST /api/pull
POST /api/show
GET  /api/tags
GET  /api/version
GET  /health
GET  /static/<path:filename>
POST /v1/audio/transcriptions
POST /v1/cancel
POST /v1/chat/completions
POST /v1/embeddings
GET  /v1/models
```

### Totals
- **21 explicit route decorators** (9 on `app`, 12 on `ollama_app`).
- **2 built-in static routes** (one per app) → **23 route registrations** total.
- **18 unique paths**, of which **3 are dual-mode** (served by both apps, both ports): `/api/embed`, `/api/embeddings`, `/v1/chat/completions`.

### What is NOT a route (checked, excluded)
- No `@app.errorhandler` / `@ollama_app.errorhandler` (grep clean).
- No `add_url_rule` / Blueprint / method-shortcut decorators (`.get()`/`.post()`/etc.) or dynamic route registration — the only `.route(`-looking hits are an SSE-splitter helper (lines 4882/4908/4923) and the `_route_request` routing helper (line 5001).
- `_debug_openai` (line 5202, `@app.before_request`) and `_debug_ollama` (line 5727, `@ollama_app.before_request`) are request hooks, not routes.
- Flask auto-adds HEAD (to GET routes) and OPTIONS (to all routes); listed methods are the hand-declared ones.

Main caveat: the two Flask apps aren't importable outside the repo in this environment (no `flask` installed), so route registration is verified against Flask's source semantics (scaffold.py/flask/app.py), not by running `app.url_map`. ollama_app's static route is registered but serves nothing (cwd fallback).
</task_result>
</task>
